glosses: past active perfective participle of онеме́ть (onemétʹ)
действ. прич. прош. вр. от онеметь
Physically unable to feel, not having the power of sensation.

examples.text: fingers numb with cold
legs numb from kneeling

glosses: Emotionally unable to feel or respond in a normal way.

examples.text: numb with shock; numb with boredom

[…] when we know that hundreds are rendered homeless every day, and countless thousands are killed and wounded, men and boys mowed down like a field of grain, and with as little compunction, we grow a little bit numb to human misery.
[…] seeing the dog—somehow that made me feel again. I’d been too dazed, too numb, to feel the full viciousness of it.
[…] he submitted […] as a traitor, his mind numb with vodka, submits to a firing squad.

glosses: Dumb or stupid.
Causing numbness.

examples.text:
[…] he did lap me
Even in his own garments, and gave himself,
All thin and naked to the numb cold night.

glosses: To cause to become numb (physically or emotionally).

examples.text: The dentist gave me novocaine to numb my tooth before drilling, thank goodness.
When I first heard the news, I was numbed by the shock.

The ravviſh danke of clumzie vvinter ramps / The fluent ſummers vaine: and drizling ſleete / Chilleth the vvan bleak cheek of the numd earth, / VVhilſt ſnarling guſts nibble the iuyceles leaues, / From the nak't ſhuddring branch; […]
But her main concern is the hard seating that numbs the nether regions.

glosses: To cause (a feeling) to be less intense.

examples.text: He turned to alcohol to numb his pain.
[I was] thankful for the pain, which helped to numb my terror.

glosses: To cause (the mind, faculties, etc.) to be less acute.

examples.text: […] hunger, fatigue, and despairing hopelessness had numbed his brain […]
The noise, the rush of air past our ears, was positively terrific. It actually seemed to numb the senses and make it almost impossible to take in impressions at all.
[The sofa] exhaled a breath of trapped ancient farts, barf-smell, and antiseptic, the parfum de asylum that gradually numbed my nose to all other scents on the ward.

glosses: To become numb (especially physically).

examples.text: […] after fumbling with numbing fingers for ten or fifteen minutes, he waved his hand with a gesture of despair […]
[…] once more his feet began to numb. Again he got down and stamped the circulation going, but as soon as he began to ride again they numbed.

glosses: Unable to speak; lacking power of speech.

examples.text: deaf, dumb, and blind
His younger brother was born dumb, and communicated with sign language.
to unloose the very tongues even of dumb creatures

The country people frequently ſay,—How can you treat a poor dumb beaſt ill; and a ſtreſs is very properly laid on the word dumb; for dumb they appear to thoſe who do not obſerve their looks and geſtures; but God, who takes care of every thing, underſtands their language...
We are dumb and we would talk

It is true, there is Turkish of which I had picked up a few phrases, and there is Chinese of which I did not understand a single word. But I had no fear of remaining dumb in Turkestan and the Celestial Empire.
Deaf and blind and dumb and born to follow / What you need is someone strong to guide you

glosses: Not talkative; taciturn or unwilling to speak.
Having no input or voice in running things.

examples.text: Life was never a May-game for men; in all times the lot of the dumb-millions born to toil was defaced with manifold sufferings, injustices, heavy burdens, avoidable and unavoidable; not play at all, but hard work that made the sinews sore, and the heart sore.

glosses: Unaccompanied by words or speech, silent, wordless.

examples.text: dumb show

Since you are tongue-tied and so loath to speak
In dumb significants proclaim your thoughts

O let my books be then the eloquence
And dumb presagers of my speaking breast […]
to pierce into the dumb past

glosses: Not producing any sound, silent.
Stupid.

examples.text: You are so dumb! You don't even know how to make toast!

glosses: Pointless, foolish, lacking intellectual content or value.

examples.text: Brendan had the dumb job of moving boxes from one conveyor belt to another.
This is dumb! We're driving in circles! We should have asked for directions an hour ago!

glosses: Lacking some functionality or property ordinarily characteristic of its kind.
Not equipped with intelligent behavior or processing capabilities of its own.
Lacking brightness or clearness as a colour; dim, dull.

examples.text: Her stern, which was painted of a dumb white or dun color.

glosses: To silence.

examples.text:
[…] what I would have spoke
Was beastly dumbed by him.
The paralysis of the Northern conscience, the dumbing of the Northern voice, were coming to an end.

glosses: To make stupid.

examples.text: I think she's dumbing us down, so we won't be smarter than her.

glosses: To represent as stupid.

examples.text: Bad-mouthing Neanderthals […] is symptomatic of a need to exclude and even demonize. […] I suggest that the unproven dumbing of the Neanderthals is an example of the same cultural preconception.

glosses: To reduce the intellectual demands of.

examples.text: The ensuing storm caused the department to lower the bar—amid protests that this was dumbing the test down—so that only 80 percent of urban kids would fail.

glosses: Very, extremely.

examples.text: "What, you don't like your food?" Russo asks. ¶ "Are you kidding? It's dumb good."

Yo this shit is crazy how these females are making these doctors rich. My baby moms Miracle is getting surgery in a week or so. She's flying out to Colombia. That shit really baffles me as far as she's concerned, because Miracle is already dumb thick. I'm like damn ma, how big do you want your ass to be?

glosses: An intensifier expressing contempt; damn, damned.

examples.text: Pap came to stand beside her and watched the two play. "That pup has just plum' fell in love with our Sammy, an' Sam's real took by him," Pap said. "It's a dumb shame, too. I talked to Jim, but he's not of a mind to sell."
